title: Draft: Add new dissector API for non-heuristic dissectors returning bool.
description:
A "new-style" dissector returns true if it recognized the packet as one
for its protocol and false if not, regardless of whether it was handed
an empty tvbuff or not.

The dissector is passed, as the data argument, a pointer to a
dissector_data_t. That is a structure that currently contains:

* a void * that points to data that the calling dissector wants to pass
  to it - that's the equivalent of the old void * data argument;
* a void * that points to data associated with the dissector handle when
  the handle is created - that's the equivalent of the old void * cb_data
  argument;
* an int that's initialized to the captured length of the packet being
  handed to the disssector and that the dissector should, if it doesn't
  dissect the entire tvbuff, set to the number of bytes that it did
  dissect.

This allows a new-style dissector to independently indicate whether it
accepted the packet and how much of that packet was dissected, so that,
if the tvbuff is empty, and that's a valid packet (as it is with sme
protocols, such as the Echo and Time protocols), and the dissector
accepts it, it can indicate that it did so.

New APIs are added for *calling* dissectors as well; they return a bool
that indicates whether the dissector accepted the packet, and also take
a possibly-null int * that, if not null, points to a variable that will
be set to the number of bytes dissected.  Most dissector calls appear
not to care about the number of bytes dissected, they just care whether
the packet was dissected or not, so those calls, if converted to the new
APIs, would just pass NULL; the few that do would pass a pointer to a
variable that will be set to the amount dissected.

The existing APIs for calling dissectors can handle all three types of
dissector; they will return the number of bytes dissected, so they can't
distinguish, even with a new-style dissector, between "not accepted by
the dissector" and "accepted by the dissector but the tvbuff is empty".

The new APIs for calling dissectors can handle all three types of
dissector; for old-style dissectors, they will return true if the
dissector returns a non-zero value and false if it returns zero, and, if
the pointer to the "amount dissected" variable is non-null, set the
value of that variable to the return value of the old-style dissector.

This should allow dissectors to be converted over time to be new-style
dissectors and to use the new APIs without having a giant "flag day".

At some point, we should introduce new-style heuristic dissectors that
have the same signature as new-style non-heuristic dissectors, with a
similar mechanism to allow conversion to be done over time. This would
allow heuristic dissectors to get callback data and to indicate how much
data they dissected, and would also allow the same dissector function to
be used as a heuristic dissector and a non-heuristic dissector.

Fixes #12368.

Is a useful step towards fixing some bugs mentioned in {transitive
closure of "mentioned in that bug"}.

"new-style" here refers to the current style (called new-style a couple decades ago) not the new-new-style being introduced in this MR. This comment might need to be updated, I suppose, now that the old-old-style doesn't exist and the old-new-style is about to become the new-old-style.
I also would strongly suggest to stay away from naming conventions based on temporal order, since these always trend their significance diluting over time.

> "new-style" here refers to the current style (called new-style a couple decades ago) not the new-new-style being introduced in this MR.No, "new-style" here refers to the style introduced in this MR.  The only remnant of "new-style" referring to the current style that I found with a quick search for "new-" preceded by a * (to eliminate constructs such as `new->frobozz`) was in the packet-pana.c dissector; I fixed that (which was confusingly using "new-style" to mean "non-heuristic").

> This comment might need to be updated,

The comment in question was introduce in this commit, so it should be up-to-date.

I *did* remove some comments using "new-style" in the old-style sense. :-)

> I also would strongly suggest to stay away from naming conventions based on temporal order, since these always trend their significance diluting over time.

Once the last old-style dissector and the last old-style dissector call are removed, the old-style dissector call routines will be removed, and he `new_` will e removed from all the routines.  The intent is *not* to have the old-style stuff remain forever.

> I _did_ remove some comments using "new-style" in the old-style sense. :-)

And decided to do so in a separate merge request, !20240, as the comment isn't even correct for the *current* version of the code, for more reasons than just using "new-style" in a now out-of-date sense - the distinction isn't between "new-style" and heuristic, it's between non-heuristic and heuristic, and the heuristic dissection is done by a wrapper around the non-heuristic dissector.

With this change plus the suggested fix for #20582, it would be possible to use the same function for both purposes.

The problem is that the comment got the two dissector types backwards, as those routines are old-style caller routines, so they call *old*-style dissectors and return their return value, and call *new*-style dissectors and return the amount of data consumed by the dissector if the dissector returns `true` and return 0 if the dissector returns `false`.

But there need to be new-style *direct* callers as well as the new-style *indirect* `new_dissector_try...` routines.

commits_data.title: Add new dissector API for non-heuristic dissectors returning bool.
commits_data.message:
Add new dissector API for non-heuristic dissectors returning bool.

A "new-style" dissector returns true if it recognized the packet as one
for its protocol and false if not, regardless of whether it was handed
an empty tvbuff or not.

The dissector is passed, as the data argument, a pointer to a
dissector_data_t. That is a structure that currently contains:

* a void * that points to data that the calling dissector wants to pass
  to it - that's the equivalent of the old void * data argument;
* a void * that points to data associated with the dissector handle when
  the handle is created - that's the equivalent of the old void * cb_data
  argument;
* an int that's initialized to the captured length of the packet being
  handed to the disssector and that the dissector should, if it doesn't
  dissect the entire tvbuff, set to the number of bytes that it did
  dissect.

This allows a new-style dissector to independently indicate whether it
accepted the packet and how much of that packet was dissected, so that,
if the tvbuff is empty, and that's a valid packet (as it is with sme
protocols, such as the Echo and Time protocols), and the dissector
accepts it, it can indicate that it did so.

New APIs are added for *calling* dissectors as well; they return a bool
that indicates whether the dissector accepted the packet, and also take
a possibly-null int * that, if not null, points to a variable that will
be set to the number of bytes dissected.  Most dissector calls appear
not to care about the number of bytes dissected, they just care whether
the packet was dissected or not, so those calls, if converted to the new
APIs, would just pass NULL; the few that do would pass a pointer to a
variable that will be set to the amount dissected.

The existing APIs for calling dissectors can handle all three types of
dissector; they will return the number of bytes dissected, so they can't
distinguish, even with a new-style dissector, between "not accepted by
the dissector" and "accepted by the dissector but the tvbuff is empty".

The new APIs for calling dissectors can handle all three types of
dissector; for old-style dissectors, they will return true if the
dissector returns a non-zero value and false if it returns zero, and, if
the pointer to the "amount dissected" variable is non-null, set the
value of that variable to the return value of the old-style dissector.

This should allow dissectors to be converted over time to be new-style
dissectors and to use the new APIs without having a giant "flag day".

At some point, we should introduce new-style heuristic dissectors that
have the same signature as new-style non-heuristic dissectors, with a
similar mechanism to allow conversion to be done over time. This would
allow heuristic dissectors to get callback data and to indicate how much
data they dissected, and would also allow the same dissector function to
be used as a heuristic dissector and a non-heuristic dissector.

Fixes #12368.

Is a useful step towards fixing some bugs mentioned in {transitive
closure of "mentioned in that bug"}.
